title: rw-private-dr: retention pruning + idempotent re-run safeguards (protect latest-known-good)
author: Connor O'Brien
release_notes: Private DR toolkit: backup retention pruning is now supported with guardrails to prevent deletion of latest-known-good backups; re-running backup create is idempotent and will not create duplicate snapshots for the same run id.
description:
Context: Operators requested safer retention handling for scheduled backups and a predictable outcome when re-running `rw-private-dr backup create` after transient failures (network blips, throttling, pod eviction). Today, the job may leave partial artifacts and repeated attempts can create duplicate prefixes; additionally, manual cleanup is error-prone and we have no hard guardrails against deleting the last usable snapshot.

What this PR does: Adds a retention pruning module for backup repositories and introduces idempotent re-run behavior for `backup create`. Pruning is conservative by default and contains explicit safety checks to ensure we never delete the "latest known good" snapshot (LKG) and never prune below a minimum viable set of backups.

Key changes: 1) Retention pruning (`rw-private-dr backup prune` + optional `--prune` on create): - Supports time-based retention (`retain_days`) and count-based retention (`retain_last`). - Supports an explicit "never prune" allowlist via backup metadata labels (e.g., `retain=forever`). - Implements an LKG protection rule: backups marked as `status=verified` are candidates for LKG; the most recent verified backup is pinned and cannot be deleted by pruning unless `--unsafe-allow-delete-lkg` is provided (not wired into scheduled jobs; only for break-glass workflows). - Adds a "minimum remaining" rule (`min_remaining_verified`, default 1) to prevent pruning into an unrecoverable state.

2) Idempotent re-run semantics for `backup create`: - Introduces a per-run identifier `run_id` (UUID) written to the repository and embedded into the backup manifest. - If a backup is re-run with the same `run_id`, the tool will: (a) detect existing finalized artifacts and exit success without re-uploading; (b) detect partial artifacts (missing manifest, missing checksums, missing DB dump) and attempt repair/resume; (c) refuse to overwrite a finalized backup created by a different `run_id` under the same timestamp prefix.

3) Partial backup handling + cleanup: - Adds an atomic "finalize" step that writes `manifest.json` last; prune only considers backups with a valid manifest and `state=finalized` unless `--include-partials` is explicitly passed (default false). - Adds a "stale partial cleanup" path: partial uploads older than `partial_ttl_hours` (default 24h) are eligible for deletion, but only if doing so won’t remove the only verified backup.

4) Safety rails and UX: - `--dry-run` for pruning to print what would be deleted and why (including the rule that selected each deletion). - All deletions require a single confirmation prompt unless `--yes` is provided (CronJobs will use `--yes`). - Emits structured logs with stable keys (e.g., `action=prune_delete`, `reason=retain_last_exceeded`, `pinned=lkg`).

Testing: - Unit tests cover selection logic for time/count retention, LKG pinning, and minimum remaining verified rule. - Integration-ish tests mock an S3 repository layout and validate: idempotent re-run does not duplicate uploads; partials are not pruned by default; dry-run output is deterministic.

Rollout notes: - This is wired into the CLI and config schema but NOT auto-enabled for existing clusters; operators can opt-in by setting `backup.retention.*` in config or by adding `--prune` to CronJobs (helm work tracked separately). - Documentation will be updated in a follow-up PR to `redwood-docs` to include examples and recommended defaults.

Security: - No changes to encryption scheme; pruning honors existing server-side encryption settings. - The tool does not log object keys that may contain customer identifiers; object paths are redacted in default log level, and only surfaced in `--debug`.

Refs: ENG-4821 (Day-2 Ops Toolkit), ENG-4841 (backup create implementation), and DR game day feedback re: "do not ever delete our last usable backup".

conversation:
Michael Nguyen (review): The min remaining verified rule is great. Can we make sure we never consider a backup "verified" unless `backup verify` has completed successfully? Right now it looks like create can mark it verified when checksums are present.
Connor O'Brien (author): Good catch. Adjusted: `backup create` now sets `state=finalized` only; `status=verified` is only written by `backup verify`. Added a test to ensure verified is never set during create.

Rafael Mendes (review): During game days we saw operators rerun create without remembering flags. What happens if they rerun without providing the same run_id? Also, are we safe if two CronJobs overlap?
Connor O'Brien (author): If run_id not provided we generate one and store it locally in the job logs only; rerun will create a new backup prefix and the old partial will be eligible for stale cleanup after TTL (but won’t be pruned as a valid backup). Overlap: we still rely on helm-level concurrency safeguards; however I added a repo-level lock file best-effort (`.rw-lock`) that causes the second run to back off with a clear message. It’s not a distributed lock but helps for the common case.

Marcus Lin (review): Please confirm we never delete the LKG by default, and that the break-glass flag is clearly named as unsafe and not used in automation.
Connor O'Brien (author): Confirmed. Planner pins newest verified backup as LKG; all deletion candidates are filtered against it. The only override is `--unsafe-allow-delete-lkg` and it is not referenced from any example CronJob; also added an explicit warning log + requires `--yes`.

Sahana Iyer (review): CI flaked once in mock-s3 test due to nondeterministic ordering. Can we sort inputs before printing dry-run?
Connor O'Brien (author): Fixed. Repository listing results are now sorted by (created_at, backup_id). Dry-run output is stable; updated tests accordingly.

Rafael Mendes (review): One more: partial cleanup should not delete recent partials, but also shouldn’t grow without bound for a stuck cluster. Default TTL=24h seems fine; can we add a metric/log counter so observability can alert later?
Connor O'Brien (author): Added structured log `partial_cleanup_deleted_count` and `partial_cleanup_skipped_count` with reasons. Metrics plumbing will be in a follow-up in observability-pack; linked in ENG-4869.
Michael Nguyen (approval): Looks good after the verified-state fix. Approved.
Marcus Lin (approval): Approved with the unsafe flag naming + warnings.
Rafael Mendes (approval): Approved. Please call out in release notes that concurrency protection is still helm-level for now.
Merged by Connor O'Brien via squash merge.
